lessons: Orientation first: the introduction states the result and why a specialist cares, then the one mechanism, then precisely what is new against each named antecedent (with the antecedent's own hypotheses and outputs), then a roadmap of every section and appendix; each section opens with one sentence saying where it is going. Pay for it by moving alternative proofs and long constant derivations to the long record.

Statement fidelity table: for every central result linked to Lean, say in the appendix whether the formal statement is the same, stronger or partial, what exactly differs, whether it is compared or only built, and whether the relation has been reviewed and is current. Formal proofs drift to nearby, easier statements; the reader should not have to discover the gap.

A counterexample row must refute the exact shortcut named in the row; when one example defeats a neighbouring shortcut (a total order) and another defeats the stated one (bounded-error fixed predicate), name both shortcuts and attach each example to the one it refutes.
When abbreviating a randomized construction, keep every branch of the rule (for example the fallback when nothing is discovered); a symmetry claim about the marginal law depends on it.

Credit sentences must match the antecedent's object: distinguish who proved hardness of the explicit problem from who proved the optimal separation by another family, and distinguish a lemma pair from a paper's headline theorem with different hypotheses.
A link that advertises a full proof must land at the start of the argument, not at its final assembly; give separate links for sub-arguments the sentence names.
A Lean link highlight must cover the complete declaration type; a range-exists check passes highlights that stop at a let-binding before the conclusion.

Describe a formal endpoint by what its type says (for example a joint success-and-compliance bound over finitely many seeds) and state the ordinary step that turns it into the paper's statement, rather than calling it the paper's lemma.

Check page count after every structural addition; LaTeX keep-together rules for short tables can push whole tables and the reference list to new pages, so make long tables breakable rather than cutting content.
